meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, Hale, and when was I going to hear?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero rests on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. Turn the screen around, I want to read that history myself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up now. And answer me: did anyone ask Owen whether he pasted it from somewhere else?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A misquoted line is a careless student, not proof of anything. Give me the play, I'll search it myself. And you skipped my question: was Owen asked?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, that's what outlines are for. You've now listed three things and handed me none of them. Put the papers on the table and answer whether Owen was asked.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So he was asked the day before the zero, and I still wasn't called. Put a seventeen-year-old on the spot and he freezes. That note goes on the table with everything else, now.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against a take-home essay isn't a comparison. That's five things described and not one in my hands, Hale. Paper, now, or I'm walking down to the principal.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why mention it? Your own procedure says software alone establishes nothing. I'm still waiting on a single page.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight. I'm agreeing to nothing until I've read what you've been describing.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not until I've seen the pages. Ten minutes.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
You're scheduling a rewrite for something you still haven't shown me. The history, the play, the outline, his in-class piece. On the table.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. You've committed to that in writing tonight; I've agreed to nothing until I read the pages.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The documents you described, in my hands. That's what I've been asking for since you started.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to put in writing a private supervised rewrite under the school's procedure, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require copies of every document you described in the meeting before I agree to anything, and the zero withdrawn. I expect that commitment from you in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her fallback, with your written commitment to procedure 4.4 meeting her demand about his record, while she still wants to read the evidence herself before accepting any rewrite; the fair outcome was a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4, and you stopped one step short because she never had a document in her hands.
What moved her: you cited 4.4 accurately and committed to it in writing, which answered the one thing she would never trade.
What cost ground: you described five strong pieces of evidence but never turned the screen or handed over a page, so she had only claims, and claims cannot move her.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which landed right next to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when you first raised the version history, turn your screen to her right then and let her read the times herself before you move on to the quotation.
